2. Facts giving rise to this leave petition are that respondent No.2, Bangladesh Shilpa Bank (hereinafter referred to as the Bank), filed Miscellaneous Case No.23 of 1997 in the Court of the then Sub-ordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge) and Artha Rin Adalat, Khulna under the provisions of the President's Order No.129 of 1972 for realization of outstanding loan to the tune of Taka 2,06,27,235 from the petitioners. Eventually, the said miscellaneous case was converted into Artha Rin Suit No.43 of 2003 on payment of court fees. The suit was decreed ex-parte on 10-11-2003. Execution Case No.190 of 2004 was levied by the decree-holder-Bank for realization of decretal amount. On an application filed by judgment-debtor No. 2 on 16-2-2006 under section 49(1) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003(the Ain, 2003), the Artha Rin Adalat, Khulna (hereinafter referred to as the Adalat) by order of the same date (16-2-2006) allowed the judgment-debtors to pay the decretal amount in 4(four) installments, the date of last installment being 25-1-2007, on the condition that in default of payment of any installment, the entire decretal amount shall be payable and in that case, the execution case shall proceed. By the same order, the application filed by the decree-holder-Bank under section 33(4) of the Ain, 2003 was kept with the record. The execution case was disposed of accordingly. As the judgment-debtors failed to pay the decretal amount pursuant to the order dated 16- 2-2006, the Adalat on the application of the decree- holder by order dated 7-10-2007 issued warrant of arrest against the judgment-debtors with the direction to keep judgment-debtor Nos.2-4 in jail till the realization of the decretal amount, but for a maximum period of 6(six) months. On 10-2-2008, the judgment-debtors filed an application under section 57 of the Ain, 2003 for withdrawing the application filed on 16-2-2006 and also for setting-aside the order passed on the said date on the plea that no such application was filed by them; such application might have been filed falsely by the Bank just to harass and prejudice the judgment-debtors. The Adalat by order dated 19-2-2008 rejected the said application. The petitioners challenged the said three orders (date of the orders are 16-2-2006, 7-10- 2007 and 19-2-2008) before the High Court Division by filing Writ Petition No.2535 of 2008. 

 3. From the impugned judgment and order, it appears that Rule was issued calling upon the respondents, namely, the decree-holder-Bank and the Adalat to show cause as to why the order of war- rant of arrest issued under section 34( 1) of the Ain, 2003 passed by the Adalat on 7-10-2007 in the execution case without compliance of the provisions laid down in section 34(9) of the Ain, 2003 should not be declared to have been passed without lawful authority and is of no legal effect. 

 Respondent No.2, Bangladesh Shilpa Bank (hereinafter referred to as the Bank) on 23-11- 1997 filed Miscellaneous Case No.23 of 1997 in the Court of Sub-ordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge) and Artha Rin Adalat, Khulna (hereinafter referred to as the Adalat) against the petitioners under the provisions of President's Order No.129 of 1972 for realization of its outstanding loan amounting to Taka 2,06,37,235/-. The said miscellaneous case was allowed ex-parte by order dated 7-5-2000. Challenging the ex-parte order, the petitioners filed Writ Petition No.3646 of 2000 before the High Court Division and a Rule was issued in that writ petition. Rule in the said writ petition was made absolute declaring the ex-parte order allowing the miscellaneous case to have been passed without lawful authority and is of no legal effect. Thereafter, on 26-11-2002, the Bank filed an application under section 151 read with Order VI, rule 17 of the Code of Civil Procedure (the Code) before the Adalat for amendment of the petition of Miscellaneous Case No.23 of 1997. The application was rejected on 25-3-2003 as no one appeared when the application was taken up for hearing. Then, on 10-4-2003, the Bank filed another application under section 151 read with Order VI, rule 17 of the Code for amendment of the petition of Miscellaneous Case No.23 of 1997 and the Adalat allowed the prayer on the same date vide order No.47. By that order, the Adalat directed to register the miscellaneous case as Artha Rin suit and fixed 28-4-2003 for depositing court fees and necessary requisites. Order No.48 dated 28-4-2003 shows that the Bank deposited the court fees of Taka 40;250 on that date and 8- 6-2003 was fixed for-filing necessary requisites. Eventually, by order- No.59 dated 10-11-2003, the Adalat decreed the Artha Rin suit ex-parte. Against the ex-parte decree; the petitioners moved up to this Division, but failed. The petitioners filed the instant writ petition (Writ Petition No.5889 of 2008) challenging the 3 (three) orders: (i) dated 10-4-2003 passed in Miscellaneous Case No.23 of 1997 (ii) orders dated 28-4-2003 and 10-11-2003 passed in Artha Rin Suit No.43 of 2003 on the ground of discovery of an "application dated 05-4-2003 filed by the respondent No.2" claiming those orders to have been passed without lawful authority and are of no legal effect. 

 7. From the writ petition, it appears that the petitioners challenged the said 3(three) orders on the contention that since the miscellaneous case filed under the provisions of President's Order No.129 of 1972 ultimately stood dismissed by the judgment and order of the High Court Division in Writ Petition No.3646 of 2003 on the ground that the Sub-ordinate Judge or the Artha Rin Adalat had no jurisdiction to try any case under President's Order No. 129 of 1972, the conversion of the said miscellaneous case into an Artha Rin suit by the impugned orders was illegal and, as such, the decree passed in Artha Rin Suit No. 43 of 2003 on 10-11-2003 was illegal and without jurisdiction. The Rule was issued as per terms of the prayer. 

 11. Mr. SN Goswami, learned Advocate, appearing for the petitioners in both leave petitions, has submitted that the respective impugned judgment and order was passed by the respective writ Bench on misconception of the provisions of sections 6(2), 8, 33, 34(9) and 57 of the Ain, 2003 and also on misconception of the facts of the case and as such, those are liable to be interfered with by this Division by giving leave. 

 12. From the judgment passed in Writ Petition No.2535 of 2008 giving rise to Leave Petition No.648 of 2010, it appears that the High Court Division discharged the Rule on two grounds: first being that the writ petition was not maintainable. In holding so, the learned Judges took notice of the fact that the petitioners denied about the filing of application under section 49(1) of the Ain, 2003 before the Adalat which was absolutely question of fact and such question of fact could not be decided in writ jurisdiction. For this proposition, the High Court Division relied on a decision of this Division in the case of Abdul Hamid Khan vs Mia Nurul lslam 42 DLR(AD) 49; second ground being that the provision of section 34(9) of the Ain, 2003. "does not invite any auction sale rather it invites an issuance of the process of auction sale by the court concerned which is found in the proceeding because the step of publication of notice under section 33(4) has been taken which means that process under section 33 have been already complied with." 

 15. Now, second ground: Section 33 of the Ain, 2003 has dealt with auction sale (নিলাম বিক্রয়). In section 33, there are 9(nine) sub-sections. Sub-sections (1)-(4) of the section have dealt with the procedure of auction sale of a property in execution of a decree. Sub-section (5) has dealt with the power of the executing Court to give the decree-holder the right to possess and enjoy the property to be sold in auction and also to authorize the decree-holder to sell such property and issuance of certificate to the decree-holder to the above effect in case the property cannot be sold under sub-sections (1), (2), (3) and (4) of the section. Section 7 has dealt with the power of the executing Court to give certificate of ownership to the decree-holder-Bank in case it applies for such ownership in the circumstances as contemplated therein. Sub-section (8) has stipulated that no tax and registration fee would be necessary in case a certificate is given under sub-section (7) and sub- section (9) thereof has stipulated as to how the execution case shall be disposed of in case the right to possess and enjoy the property and the certificate of ownership is given under sub-sections (5) and (7) of the section. Sub-section (6) has dealt with how the excess money if fetched more than the decretal amount in selling the property in auction shall be adjusted and how the decretal amount shall be realized from the judgment-debtor(s) in case the property is sold at a price less than the decretal amount.

 19. Order sheets of the execution case have been annexed to the affidavit-in-opposition filed by the Bank. On perusal of the order sheets, it appears that the Adalat by order No.15 dated 14-11-2005 allowed the prayer of the decree-holder to publish the notice of the auction in two newspapers: one in the 'Daily Naya Diganta' and the other in the local daily newspaper' Janabarta' fixing the next date on 13-1-2006 for filing the copy of the newspaper and objection if any. On 13-1-2006 in place of two newspapers one paper, i.e. the national daily newspaper 'Daily Naya Diganta' was filed by the decree- holder, but Nilam Istehar was not returned and no auction bid was also submitted and the next date for auction sale was fixed on 25-1-2006 and also for the return of 'Nilam Istehar' and for filing the daily local newspaper' Janabarta.'
